intro.title: Discover Salinas y Arenales de San Pedro del Pinatar
intro.description: The Salinas y Arenales de San Pedro del Pinatar Regional Park is a stunning natural reserve located in the Region of Murcia, Spain. This unique ecosystem combines salt flats, sand dunes, and Mediterranean coastal habitats, making it a paradise for birdwatchers and nature lovers.

visitGuide.title: Visit Tips
items: The park is accessible year-round with free admission.
Bring binoculars for excellent birdwatching opportunities.
Wear comfortable shoes for walking on sandy paths.
Visit during sunrise or sunset for the best photography.

alsoKnownAs.title: Highlights
items: Sand dunes of Playa de la Llana

sections.title: Historical Background
sections.content: The salt flats of San Pedro del Pinatar have been in use since ancient times, with evidence of salt production dating back to the Roman era. The park was officially designated as a Regional Park to protect its unique natural and cultural heritage.

sections.title: Ecosystem & Geography
sections.content: The park covers 856 hectares and includes salt flats, coastal lagoons, sand dunes, and pine forests. It serves as a crucial stopover for migratory birds along the Mediterranean flyway.

sections.title: Flora & Fauna
sections.content: The park hosts over 130 species of birds throughout the year, including flamingos, avocets, terns, and gulls. The flora includes salt-tolerant plants, dunes vegetation, and Mediterranean scrubland.

sections.title: Conservation Status
sections.content: The park is protected under multiple international designations: it is a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance, part of the Natura 2000 network as both a Special Protection Area (ZEPA) and a Site of Community Importance (LIC).

sections.title: Visitor Facilities
sections.content: The park features several observation points, walking trails, and an interpretation center. There are information panels along the routes, and guided tours are available upon request.

hours.title: Visiting Hours
hours.bestTimeSpring: Spring: Bird migration season, pleasant temperatures
hours.bestTimeSummer: Summer: Early morning or evening to avoid heat
hours.bestTimeWinter: Winter: Mild weather, ideal for walking
hours.tip: The park is open 24/7. The best birdwatching is during early morning or late afternoon.

tickets.title: Admission Information
tickets.parkingPrice: Free parking available at designated areas
tickets.guidedPrice: Available upon request at the interpretation center

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: Approximately 45km from Murcia city center. Take the A-7 motorway towards Cartagena, then exit towards San Pedro del Pinatar.
transport.fromStationDesc: About 20km from Cartagena. Accessible by bus or car via the RM-3 and AP-7.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Murcia International Airport (RMU) is approximately 15km away. Alicante Airport (ALC) is about 75km north.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Interurban buses connect San Pedro del Pinatar with Murcia and Cartagena. Local buses serve the town.
transport.walkingDesc: The park is accessible on foot from San Pedro del Pinatar town center (approximately 2km to the main entrance).
transport.drivingDesc: Accessible by car via the AP-7 or RM-3. Follow signs to 'Salinas' or 'Parque Regional'.

route.title: Recommended Route
route.overview: A scenic walk through the salt flats and coastal dunes.
steps: Start at the main parking area near the interpretation center
Walk along the southern observation trail for birdwatching
Visit the salt flats and observe traditional salt harvesting
Continue to the dunes of Playa de la Llana
End at the northern lookout point for sunset views

spots.title: Salt Flats Lookout
spots.description: The view of the salt flats with pink waters during evaporation season creates stunning reflections, especially at sunrise.

spots.title: Bird Hide (Observatorio)
spots.description: One of several birdwatching hides around the lagoons. Perfect for capturing flamingos and other wading birds.

spots.title: Playa de la Llana Dunes
spots.description: The sand dunes offer beautiful textures and coastal views, ideal for landscape and nature photography.

spots.title: Sunset Viewpoint
spots.description: The northern part of the park offers panoramic sunset views over the salt flats and the Mar Menor.

items.name: Carlos M.
items.text: An absolutely spectacular natural park. The variety of birds you can observe here is incredible. A must-visit if you're in the Murcia region.

items.name: Laura G.
items.text: Beautiful place for a peaceful walk. The combination of salt flats, sea, and dunes is unique. Perfect for photography enthusiasts.

items.name: Antonio R.
items.text: One of the best natural parks in the Region of Murcia. The interpretive panels are very informative, and the trails are well maintained.

items.name: Maria S.
items.text: Great place for birdwatching. We saw flamingos, avocets, and many other species. Go early in the morning for the best experience.

items.name: David L.
items.text: A hidden gem in San Pedro del Pinatar. The sunset views from the northern part of the park are breathtaking. Free entrance is a plus.

items.name: Elena F.
items.text: Perfect for a family outing. The kids enjoyed the interpretive center and looking at the birds through the binoculars. Very educational.

officialManagement.title: About Salinas y Arenales
officialManagement.text: The Salinas y Arenales de San Pedro del Pinatar Regional Park is a protected natural area in the Region of Murcia, Spain. The park is managed by the Regional Government of Murcia in collaboration with the San Pedro del Pinatar Town Council for conservation and public use.
